source: Francesco Orabona, arXiv:1912.13213v10, Lemma 6.33 proof, printed 80 / PDF 92.
assumptions: Every xᵢ is positive. The coefficients cᵢ are arbitrary real numbers and v is any real direction.
Each weight cᵢ is positive, and both x and y belong to K.
proofs: Differentiate each coordinate map on the positive orthant. The product rule contributes log xᵢ+1. The derivative of the finite sum adds the resulting linear functionals.

Use weights wᵢ=(xᵢ+yᵢ)/(2cᵢ), whose sum is 1 because x and y both satisfy the weighted normalization. Apply Jensen to the square at |xᵢ−yᵢ|/wᵢ to obtain the first inequality. For the second, multiply the scalar ratio inequality by cᵢ and sum. Subtracting the two ambient derivatives cancels the constant terms.
concrete_checks: With c=(1,2) and x=(1/4,3/2), the direction v=(0,1) changes the weighted mass at rate 1/2. Its derivative is 2(log(3/2)+1).

With c=(1,2), x=(1/4,3/2) and y=(3/4,1/2), both points have weighted mass 1. Their ordinary coordinate sums are 7/4 and 5/4. The two comparisons become 9/4 ≤ 5/2 ≤ (5/2)log 3. Setting y=x makes all three terms zero.
